assessments.assessment_title: Assessment 2: Digital Health Solution - Business Case (1300-1500 words)
assessments.task_description:
Purpose

To critically analyse a contemporary healthcare challenge and develop an evidence-based Business Case recommending an appropriate digital health solution. Students will apply their knowledge of digital health technologies, analyse domestic and international strategic drivers, and justify an evidence-based solution that supports safe, effective and person-centred healthcare.

Authentic Context

You are a Digital Health Consultant engaged by a healthcare organisation to investigate a contemporary healthcare challenge. Your Executive Director has requested an evidence-based Business Case recommending a digital health solution that addresses the identified challenge and aligns with the organisation's strategic priorities. Your report should demonstrate a critical understanding of the healthcare context, relevant domestic and international strategic drivers, the proposed digital health solution, and its contribution to healthcare delivery and patient outcomes.

Task

For this assessment, you will prepare a Business Case recommending an appropriate digital health solution for a healthcare organisation.

Select one of the following healthcare scenarios. Your selected scenario will form the context for your Business Case and will form the basis for your pitch in task 3. 

  1. Public Hospital - Emergency department wait times continue to exceed national benchmarks, with increasing demand for non-urgent presentations.
  2. General Practice - Patients with chronic disease experience fragmented care and inconsistent follow up.
  3. Residential Aged Care Service - Medication incidents have increased over the past 12 months, particularly during transitions of care.
  4. Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Service - Patients experience delays accessing specialist services, resulting in poorer health outcomes.
  5. Community Mental Health Service - Waiting times for mental health assessment continue to increase, limiting timely access to care.

More details of the scenarios will be provided on Blackboard site.

Using your selected scenario, identify and justify an appropriate digital health solution that addresses the healthcare challenge and supports the organisation's strategic priority. You may make reasonable assumptions where necessary; however, these should be clearly stated and supported by contemporary evidence.

Your Business Case should address the following.

1. Healthcare Challenge and Context (LO1)

Explain:

  • the healthcare challenge and why it is significant
  • the populations or stakeholders affected
  • the role of digital health in supporting safe, effective and person-centred healthcare within this context.

 

2. Strategic, Policy and Innovation Context (LO2)

Analyse:

  • the Australian strategic, policy and regulatory drivers relevant to the proposed digital health solution
  • relevant international strategies, policies, standards or technological developments influencing the proposed solution
  • how these domestic and international drivers support implementation within the selected healthcare context.

 

3. Proposed Digital Health Solution (LO3)

Apply your knowledge of digital health technologies and information systems to:

  • compare alternative digital health solutions where appropriate and explain why the proposed solution is preferred.
  • identify and explain an appropriate digital health solution
  • justify why it is the most suitable solution for the identified healthcare challenge and strategic priority

assessments.task_description:
Purpose

To develop and communicate an evidence-based implementation strategy for a digital health solution within a healthcare setting. Building on the Business Case developed in Assessment 2, students will critically analyse the potential impact of the proposed solution, evaluate factors influencing successful implementation, and present evidence-based recommendations to healthcare leaders.

Authentic Context

Following review of your Business Case, the Executive Leadership Team has shortlisted your proposed digital health solution for further consideration.

You have been invited to present your proposal to the Executive Leadership Team. Your presentation should demonstrate why the proposed solution should be implemented, how implementation could be supported, and how its impact could be evaluated.

Following your presentation, you will respond to questions from the Executive Leadership Team to clarify and justify your recommendations.

Task

Using the same healthcare scenario and digital health solution investigated in Assessment 2, prepare a 8 to 10 minute presentation supported by PowerPoint slides.

 Your presentation should address the following.

 1. Potential Impact on Healthcare Delivery (LO4)

Critically analyse how the proposed digital health solution is expected to influence healthcare delivery.

Your analysis should consider:

  • how the solution may change the delivery of healthcare services
  • how patients, clinicians and other stakeholders are likely to interact with the technology
  • how healthcare data may be collected, shared or used to support care
  • the importance of interoperability in supporting continuity of care and clinical decision making
  • the potential impact on patient outcomes, quality of care and healthcare efficiency.

 2. Implementation Considerations (LO5)

Critically evaluate the key factors that should be considered when implementing the proposed digital health solution.

Your evaluation should consider:

  • workforce education and training requirements
  • stakeholder engagement and change management
  • privacy, security and ethical considerations
  • accessibility and equity
  • resource and infrastructure requirements
  • barriers to implementation and strategies to support successful adoption.

Support your discussion with evidence from the literature and examples from contemporary healthcare practice where appropriate.

 3. Evaluating Success (LO5)

Evaluate how the success of the proposed digital health solution could be measured following implementation.

Your evaluation should consider:

  • indicators of successful implementation
  • measures of patient, clinician or organisational outcomes
  • approaches to monitoring and evaluating effectiveness
  • opportunities for continuous improvement and future development.

 4. Recommendation (LO6)

Develop and communicate an evidence-based recommendation for healthcare leaders.

Your recommendation should:

  • clearly state whether the proposed digital health solution should be implemented
  • justify your recommendation using evidence from the literature and your Business Case
  • identify the key priorities for successful implementation
  • communicate your recommendations using professional language appropriate for a healthcare leadership audience.

 Presentation Requirements

  • Individual assessment.
  • A 8 to 10 minute oral presentation supported by PowerPoint slides.
  • A 5 minute question and answer session will follow the presentation. Assessors will act as members of the Executive Leadership Team and ask questions relating to your proposed digital health solution, implementation considerations, supporting evidence and recommendations. Students should be prepared to justify and defend their proposal using contemporary evidence and examples from practice.
  • Professional presentation appropriate for a healthcare leadership audience.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeksFrom Week 1 To Week 4(27 Jul - 23 Aug)
learning_activities.topic:
Module 1 – What is Digital Health?

Covers Weeks 1 - 4 of teaching

Week 1: Introduction to digital health and health systems: Topic one will review the definitions of digital health and introduce the Australian healthcare system in the context of digital health.

Week 2: Evolution of digital health & informatics: Topic two will focus on the historical development and uptake of information communication technology, data and data exchange. 

Week 3: Underpinning of digital health: Topic three explores the factors underpinning digital health transformation of healthcare, i.e., 'what' the problems are and 'why' digital health may fix them.

Week 4: What drives digital health transformation?: Topic four will discuss the key aims and objectives of digital health.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeksFrom Week 5 To Week 8(24 Aug - 20 Sep)
learning_activities.topic:
Module 2 – Digital Health and Patient-Centred Care

Covers Weeks 5 - 8 of teaching

Week 5: Clinical decision-making & digital health (Review): Topic five explores the uses of digital health in clinical decision-making, its application in in-patient care, iEMR uses, and information systems.

Week 6: Telemonitoring and virtual care (Review): Topic six is an overview of contemporary digital technology and applications that enable independent living, ageing in place, in-home monitoring and rehabilitation in the out-patient care setting.

Week 7: Mobile devices and health (Review): Topic seven discusses consumer personal mobile devices, wearables and remote monitoring and how data can improve clinical decision-making, client engagement and health literacy. 

Week 8: AI technologies and personalised medicine (Review): Topic eight explores the secondary use of digitised health data for personalised medicine, data analytics to improve organisational efficiencies and workflow, machine learning applications for image-based diagnoses, and AR and VR-based rehabilitation therapies.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeksFrom Week 9 To Week 13(21 Sep - 01 Nov)
learning_activities.topic:
Module 3 – Population Health Goes Digital

Covers Weeks 9 - 13 of teaching

Week 9: Person-centred care (Review): Topic nine explores the importance of person-centred care, digital health literacy, its meaning, and its role in engaging patients and their communities in healthcare. It also discusses strategies for building sustainable health changes. 

Week 10: Integration and implementation: Topic ten discusses ethical, medical, legal and social considerations for implementing digital health technologies. It also explores system interoperability and design for efficient digital health implementation.

Week 11: Integration Strategies: Topic eleven explores sustainability, system interoperability, data privacy, security, compliance, and common reasons for the failure of digital clinical applications. It also overviews the funding system and economic evaluation of Australia's current digital health model.

Week 12: Global status of digital health (Review): Topic twelve compares and contrasts various countries' current global digital health adoption and emerging trends. 

Week 13: Review (Review): In the final teaching week, we will review the important concepts discussed throughout the course to assist in preparation for the final Assessment.
